title: Korean: Hangul Letters and Syllables
description: For new Korean readers: consonants, all 21 vowels, and common open and closed syllable blocks with examples. Revised Romanization is a reading aid; final consonants can change sound in connected speech.

sources.name: National Institute of Korean Language: Romanization

cards.back: g before a vowel, k finally — plain velar stop; a letter, not a word.
n — nasal consonant; a letter, not a word.
d before a vowel, t finally — plain alveolar stop; a letter, not a word.
r before a vowel, l finally — liquid consonant; a letter, not a word.
m — nasal consonant; a letter, not a word.
b before a vowel, p finally — plain bilabial stop; a letter, not a word.
s, t in an unreleased final position — plain sibilant; a letter, not a word.
silent initially, ng finally — placeholder at the start; nasal at the end; a letter, not a word.
cards.hint: Position matters: beginning versus end of a syllable.
